step_a: Infer the green rectangle, clip to its strict interior, compute same-color 4-connected components, and select the unique largest component.
intermediate: The input-derived rectangle and selected component cells, size, and color after interior clipping.
step_b: Use the selected component color to paint only zero-valued cells on the inferred rectangle border, preserving all original occupied cells.
why_b_depends_on_a: The selected color changes with rectangle scope and component identity. A larger component crossing the boundary loses its exterior cells before ranking; selecting before clipping or ignoring rectangle scope gives a different border color.

(rule!
  (let ((pts (find-color g 3)))
    (if (= (length pts) 2)
        (let* ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts))

               (c0 (min (second a) (second b))) (c1 (max (second a) (second b)))
               (inside (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                         (lambda (r c)
                           (if (and (< r0 r r1) (< c0 c c1)) (at g r c) 0))))
               (parts (filter (lambda (object) (ormap (lambda (cell) (and (< r0 (first cell) r1) (< c0 (second cell) c1))) (obj-cells object))) (objects g 0)))
               (chosen (if (null? parts) 8 (obj-color (pick-max parts obj-size)))))
          (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))] [c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))])
            (if (and (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1)) (= (at out r c) 0))
                (set-cell out r c chosen)
                out)))
        g)))
